title: Trio of Galaxies (NGC 5981, NGC 5982 and NGC 5985)
caption: The galaxy trio NGC 5981, NGC 5982 and NGC 5985, imaged by the Mayall 4-meter Telescope
credit: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and H. Schweiker (WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA)

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: Three very different galaxies line up in this image in the constellation Draco. At the top is NGC 5981, seen edge-on; in the middle is the elliptical galaxy NGC 5982; and at the bottom is the spiral galaxy NGC 5985. Together they make a distinct trio.
An elliptical galaxy is a smooth, rounded collection of stars without spiral arms, while a spiral is a flat disc with arms. An edge-on spiral appears as a thin line because we see its disc side-on.

Whether, or when, these three will merge is not clear. But NGC 5982 already shows evidence that it has recently swallowed at least one smaller galaxy. Mergers are thought to play an important part in how galaxies grow and change shape over time.

understand.summary: The Mosaic camera on the Mayall 4-meter Telescope used three filters. B is shown in blue, V in green and I in red.
filters: 436 nm · Optical B (NSF Nicholas U. Mayall 4-meter Telescope Mosaic I)
537 nm · Optical V (NSF Nicholas U. Mayall 4-meter Telescope Mosaic I)

understand.eye: These galaxies are far too faint for the eye, and the I filter records near-infrared light we cannot see.
